newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO'S COSTA SPURNS WEAH APOLOGY OFFER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO'S COSTA SPURNS WEAH APOLOGY OFFER.

text.p: Porto defender Jorge Costa, whose nose was broken by AC Milan striker George Weah, has spurned the Liberian player's offer of an apology and plans to sue him for damages, according to media reports on Sunday.
The Publico newspaper said Costa, who was attacked by Weah as the players left the field after a European Cup game in Oporto 11 days ago, could seek damages of up to $1 million.
It gave no more details of the planned suit and the player could not be contacted to comment.
Weah has admitted head-butting Costa but says the Portuguese international defender provoked him with racist insults and some dangerous tackles during the ill-tempered game.
The Liberian offered to apologise but only if Costa admitted the provocation.
"I read his declarations. He said he was sorry but he continues to lie, accusing me of being racist," Publico quoted Costa as saying.
Costa needed surgery to repair the damage to his nose and is expected to be out of the game for a month.
UEFA has suspended Weah for one match and launched an investigation into the incident.
